about: The same sampled shots of one point (the published run's own: its seed and batches), decoded by each decoder in turn on one core, 2026-11-23. The machine was busy, so read the times as ratios. The beam search is IonQ's own code (arXiv:2512.07057), at the paper's settings for each width.

bb72.says: On this code the beam search at width 8 makes fewer logical errors than BP-OSD on the same shots and decodes about four times faster; width 32 does no better than width 8. BP-OSD stays the decoder the charts rank by.

rows.label: BP-OSD (ldpc 2.4.1: product-sum BP, 30 iterations; OSD-CS order 7)
Beam search (IonQ BeamSearchDecoder 5100dc0: width 8; min-sum BP, 30 iterations then up to 10 rounds of 20)
Beam search (IonQ BeamSearchDecoder 5100dc0: width 32; min-sum BP, 40 iterations then up to 10 rounds of 30)

color5.says: On the colour code the beam search makes nearly twice as many logical errors as BP-OSD at width 8, and more at width 32, so it is not used here.
